Epigraphy: Philippe Clancier (lead) and Julien Monerie (Paris 1), Grégory Chambon (EHESS), Laurent Colonna d'Istria (Liège).

summary.text: A ~10 ha Bronze Age town on the Tanjaro River, burned at the end of the 3rd millennium BCE. Its 146 tablets and other inscribed objects are the oldest writing found in the Sulaymaniyah region and the first 3rd-millennium tablets from Iraqi Kurdistan. They are Akkadian administrative records of flour and grain, using local place and personal names. The city's ancient name is unknown; the team suggests it was a main centre, perhaps the capital, of Lullubum.
